witnesses.evidence: "Anno quintodecimo principatus Tiberiani proponit eum descendisse in civitatem Galilaeae Capharnaum" — the date and the descent to Capernaum stated as one sentence.
cited by Roth for the absence of the temptation.

records.reason: Excluded by the 3:1 → 4:31 junction. The temptation is also listed as absent in the library (Dancing with Fire §5.2).

witnesses.evidence: "Anno quintodecimo principatus Tiberiani proponit eum descendisse in civitatem Galilaeae Capharnaum" — the date and the descent to Capernaum stated as one sentence.

records.reason: Excluded by the 3:1 → 4:31 junction (Roth: unattested; difference recorded).

witnesses.evidence: "apud Nazareth quoque nihil novi notatur praedicasse, dum alio, merito unius proverbii, eiectus refertur" — the visit to Nazareth, his preaching there, and his ejection.

records.wording: NA27 (Ναζαρά). The visit and preaching are attested; the details "as was his custom", "sabbath", "stood up to read" are not.
records.position: After 4:37: Tertullian treats the Capernaum episode (4.7) before Nazareth (4.8.2), and 4:23 refers back to deeds already done at Capernaum.

witnesses.evidence: "nihil novi notatur praedicasse".

records.reason: Tertullian works through the Nazareth visit (4.8.2–3) and his whole case in book IV is that Jesus fulfils the Creator's prophets. A reading of Isaiah 61 announced as fulfilled "today" would have been his strongest proof; he says only that Jesus preached "nothing new". Silence where the passage would have served him (METHOD §3, U−).

witnesses.evidence: "cuius nemo adhuc certus de tribu, de populo, de domo" — no one yet knew his tribe, people or house.

records.reason: Tertullian argues that Jesus' descent was unknown to his hearers; "Is not this Joseph's son?" would have contradicted the Marcionite reading and served Tertullian in 4.7–4.8 and in his arguments on the birth. He does not cite it. The previous text printed 4:22a; it is removed.

witnesses.evidence: "merito unius proverbii eiectus" — thrown out because of a single proverb.

records.reason: Inside the attested Nazareth pericope. Tertullian's "unius proverbii" may refer to this saying rather than to 4:23; it cannot be decided.

witnesses.evidence: "merito unius proverbii eiectus" — thrown out because of a single proverb.

records.reason: Tertullian gives one proverb as the cause of the ejection; in canonical Luke the Elijah and Elisha sayings are what provoke the rage. Elijah sent to a Sidonian widow would also have served Tertullian's argument for the Creator's concern for the nations; it is not cited.

records.roth: present, in this position (Marc. 4.35.6; Pan. 42.11.6, sch. 48)

witnesses.evidence: ὅτε συνήντησαν οἱ δέκα λεπροί. ἀπέκοψε δὲ πολλὰ καὶ ἐποίησεν »ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς λέγων, δείξατε ἑαυτοὺς τοῖς ἱερεῦσι« καὶ ἄλλα ἀντὶ ἄλλων ἐποίησε, λέγων ὅτι »πολλοὶ λεπροὶ ἦσαν ἐν ἡμέραις Ἐλισσαίου τοῦ προφήτου καὶ οὐκ ἐκαθαρίσθη εἰ μὴ Νεεμὰν ὁ Σύρος«.
"Nunc etsi praefatus est multos tunc fuisse leprosos apud Israelem in diebus Helisaei prophetae et neminem eorum purgatum nisi Naaman Syrum…"

records.wording: Printed here, between 17:12 and 17:14, as both witnesses place it: Epiphanius within the account of the ten lepers, Tertullian as said "beforehand" (praefatus est) in the same episode (Roth, Harnack). The verse is not printed at Luke 4 (batch 1). Marcionite readings adopted: ἐν ἡμέραις ("in the days of"; Tertullian "in diebus", Epiphanius) for NA27 ἐπί, and the spelling Νεεμάν (Epiphanius). Roth: secure for both. The opening καί of Luke 4:27 belongs to its canonical context and is not printed. No witness gives the words that introduced the saying here.

records.reason: Inside the attested Nazareth pericope; Tertullian reports the ejection but not the rage.

witnesses.evidence: "manus ei iniectas… detentus et captus et ad praecipitium usque protractus".
"Nam etsi per medios evasit…"

records.roth: present (Marc. 4.7.1–7; Adam. 102,22–23; Irenaeus, Haer. 1.27.2; Hippolytus, Haer. 7.31.6)

witnesses.evidence: "Anno quintodecimo principatus Tiberiani proponit eum descendisse in civitatem Galilaeae Capharnaum" — the date and the descent to Capernaum stated as one sentence.
Asks how he could be admitted to teach in the assembly: attests the teaching in the assembly.

records.wording: NA27 without the opening Καί, which is canonical Luke's link to 4:30; the witnesses join κατῆλθεν directly to 3:1 (editorial junction). Spelling Καφαρναούμ (NA27).

witnesses.evidence: "Stupebant autem omnes ad doctrinam eius… Quoniam, inquit, in potestate erat sermo eius."
"Exclamat ibidem spiritus daemonis" — the spirit of a daimon cries out in that place (the assembly).

records.reason: Tertullian paraphrases the content of the verse (spirit of a daimon, crying out, in the assembly) before quoting 4:34. Roth lists 4:33 as unattested; the paraphrase is sufficient for A+.

witnesses.evidence: "Quid nobis et tibi est Iesu? venisti perdere nos: scio qui sis, sanctus dei." No Ἔα, no Ναζαρηνέ.

records.wording: NA27. Tertullian's quotation lacks Ἔα and Ναζαρηνέ; one witness, and Roth rates the absence of Ναζαρηνέ only "may not have been present", so NA27 is kept and the omission noted. Tertullian opens 4.8.1 with the name Nazaraeus.

witnesses.evidence: "Atquin, inquis, increpuit illum Iesus."

records.reason: Whole pericope (Simon's mother-in-law) without an attested verse (METHOD §4.3).

witnesses.evidence: "ipse mox tetigit alios, quibus manus imponens… beneficia medicinarum conferebat".

records.wording: NA27 (εἶχον, ἐθεράπευεν; checked on the page image).

witnesses.evidence: "spiritus nequam… excedebant vociferantes, Tu es filius dei… increpabantur et iubebantur tacere."

records.wording: NA27. NA27 cites McionT for its text against the addition ὁ χριστός after εἶ (A Q Θ Ψ 0102 f1.13 𝔐). κραυγάζοντα is NA27 text (κράζοντα ℵ B C …).

witnesses.evidence: "In solitudinem procedit… Detentus a turbis".
"Oportet me, inquit, et aliis civitatibus annuntiare regnum dei."

records.wording: NA27. Tertullian's order "oportet me… et aliis civitatibus" is rated very likely by Roth for δεῖ με only; word order in a Latin citation is not evidence for Greek order, so NA27 is kept.
